learn.title: Solids that come to a point
learn.body: A pyramid has a polygon base and triangular sides meeting at one point, the apex. A cone is the round version, with a circle for a base. A sphere is a ball: all points at one distance from the centre.

learn.title: One third of the prism
learn.body: A pyramid holds exactly one third of the prism with the same base and height. So $V=\frac13Bh$. A cone holds one third of the cylinder with the same base and height, so $V=\frac13\pi r^2h$.

learn.title: The sphere
learn.body: The volume of a sphere with radius $r$ is $V=\frac43\pi r^3$. It depends on the radius cubed. Doubling the radius makes the volume eight times as large.
Use the vertical height from the apex to the base, not the slant height along a face.

questions.prompt: A square pyramid has base side 6 and height 5. Find its volume.
A cone and a cylinder have the same base and height. How do their volumes compare?
choices: The cone has one third of the volume
The cone has half the volume
The cone has twice the volume
questions.explanation: The cone is $\frac13$ of the cylinder.

The volume of a pyramid is \_\_ of the matching prism.
